title: Laptop versus raytracer desktop: matched single-thread RustMage and FP32 neural benchmark

model.architecture: Unchanged production SeparateActorCritic; GRU use_cudnn=False; float32; TF32 disabled

controls: Identical released RustMage shared library, Python adapter sources, schema 131 and binding on both machines.
Same Python 3.12.14, TensorFlow 2.21.0, Keras 3.15.1, NumPy 2.5.4 and orjson 3.13.0.
One process CPU affinity: laptop CPU 1 (highest published maximum frequency); desktop WSL CPU 0.
TF intra/inter-op, OMP and BLAS threads all 1; Python observation pipeline; oneDNN disabled for neural cases.
Same trusted real-observation fixture, checkpoint and Adam state; weights and optimizer state restored before each timed repeat.
Microbenchmarks have three repeats; imports, tracing, warmups, input padding and state resets excluded.
Microbenchmarks include NumPy input handoff, host/device transfer and synchronized consumed outputs.
Backpropagation step is one real actor forward/gradient/clipping/Adam call plus one real critic call; no BPTT or PPO acceptance scans.
Full neural games use one sequential engine, batch 1, zero batching delay, fixed per-game action RNGs; trajectory writing included.
GPU computations run on the desktop; SSH network transfer is excluded from timing.

engine_summary.scope: Complete natural RustMage games through the normal Python adapter and FoundationsAggro policy, including trace hashing; no neural network.

limitations: Desktop measurements are Ubuntu in WSL2 on Windows 11; laptop is native Linux. These are usable pipeline timings, not an isolated hardware IPC comparison.
WSL does not expose the physical P/E-core mapping or per-core frequency. Supplemental 16-game CPU 8/16 checks differ by 2.6%, and remain slower than the same laptop games.
These are single-thread results, not a test of the desktop's higher core-count throughput.
Eight neural games are one timed set per device, not three repeated game sets. Their recorded neural paths and outcomes are exactly matched.
GPU forward batch 1/32 timing varies between repeats; reported values are medians with full repeat ranges retained.
Current FP32, non-cuDNN GRU implementation and one host CPU core do not measure maximum RTX 4090 throughput, mixed precision, or concurrent batched games.
Runtime tensor placement and a separate real GPU matmul/XLA-gradient test are verified; the benchmark does not contain GPU kernel profiling.

attempts.case: laptop CPU neural games, initial sandboxed attempt
attempts.note: Inference startup became unresponsive before game progress; no timing was used. SIGINT did not stop it; its own process was terminated. The same unchanged harness then completed outside the sandbox.

attempts.case: laptop CPU neural games, host rerun
attempts.note: Executed with a diagnostic traceback timer; completed before the timer fired. Host run is the reported result.

desktop_environment.setup_shell:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Source this file before running the isolated benchmark Python.
MTGO_BENCH_ROOT=/home/altf4/benchmarks/mtgo-cpu-gpu-20261024
MTGO_NVIDIA_ROOT="$MTGO_BENCH_ROOT/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia"
MTGO_CUDA_LIBS=/usr/lib/wsl/lib
for MTGO_LIB_DIR in "$MTGO_NVIDIA_ROOT"/*/lib; do
    MTGO_CUDA_LIBS="$MTGO_CUDA_LIBS:$MTGO_LIB_DIR"
done
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$MTGO_CUDA_LIBS${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
export PATH="$MTGO_NVIDIA_ROOT/cuda_nvcc/bin:$MTGO_BENCH_ROOT/venv/bin:$PATH"
export XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_cuda_data_dir=$MTGO_NVIDIA_ROOT/cuda_nvcc${XLA_FLAGS:+ $XLA_FLAGS}"
unset MTGO_LIB_DIR MTGO_CUDA_LIBS MTGO_NVIDIA_ROOT

laptop_cpu.methodology:
Matched single-core complete-game benchmark, without neural inference.

Uses the normal Python adapter and FoundationsAggro policy around the same
release RustMage library. Natural games, reset, choices, and cleanup are timed.
Compilation, imports, metadata hashing, and explicit warmups are excluded.

laptop_cpu.methodology: One host CPU core and TF intra/inter threads 1; FP32 with TF32 disabled. Identical real recorded observations and saved model/Adam state. Imports, graph traces, warmups and resets excluded. NumPy handoff and synchronized outputs included. Fixed-count paired actor/critic optimizer calls; no PPO acceptance guard or BPTT. Padding/fixture reads excluded; tensors remain NumPy inputs on every call.
laptop_cpu.graph_device_audit_scope: Empty GraphDef device fields are unknown, not proof of GPU execution. Runtime checks assert model-variable, forward-output and optimizer-norm tensor devices; calls use an explicit requested device with soft placement disabled. GPU kernel profiling is not captured.

laptop_desktop_cpu.scope:
Compare trusted local self-play reports and ordered recorded neural paths.

Numerical NN outputs (recurrent memory, values, probabilities) are excluded.
Every raw encoded observation array, chosen candidate index, and advance flag
is included. Forced actions have no trajectory sample, so this proves ordered
neural decision paths rather than a separate full engine action trace.
